basis: Inherited marrow failure; congenital skeletal/radial-ray defects occur in roughly 30-50%. Renal anomalies are usually below 30%; pigmentation alone is not damage.
Defined by cavernous malformations of cerebral capillaries; both brain and vascular anatomy are intrinsic.
Senior-Loken syndrome combines nephronophthisis progressing to renal failure with retinal degeneration and visual loss.
Inflammation throughout the uvea; infectious and immune-mediated forms account for the principal disease mechanisms.
Primary malignant soft-tissue sarcoma, commonly arising in trunk or extremity connective tissues.
Organ-specific hereditary colorectal neoplasia susceptibility; gastrointestinal is the defining target, without assuming an existing cancer or additional damage.
Microinvasive carcinoma of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Neoplasms originating in the ependymal lining of brain ventricles or the spinal central canal.
HTRA1-associated age-related macular degeneration directly damages the macula; other HTRA1 disorders are separate entities.
Dermal melanocytic lesion; scleral pigmentation in about two thirds does not itself impair function. Glaucoma and uveal melanoma are later risks.
Defined by deficient skull ossification, absent clavicles and vertebral anomalies; cleft palate affects 80-99%. Brain anomalies occur in only 5-29%.
Intellectual disability, brachydactyly and recurrent inflammatory episodes define the syndrome. Pericardial effusion and perianal abscess occur in only 5-29%.
Abnormal hemoglobin causes absent or mild hemolytic anemia; no common additional organ damage is established.
Extramammary Paget disease involves the penile surface epidermis; this cutaneous neoplasm has a dermatologic axis.
Mucinous carcinoma arising in the uterine cervix; signet-ring morphology does not imply gastrointestinal origin.
Primary ovarian failure entails loss of ovarian endocrine function, including estrogen production.
Developmental disability and cardiac malformations define it. Skeletal defects reported in 3/3 and strabismus in 2/3; dental crowding (3/3) omitted under the four-axis cap.
HERC1-related neurodevelopmental disorder; scoliosis, kyphosis, hyperlordosis and joint hypermobility were each reported in 2/2 patients.
A histologic variant of cutaneous melanoma, establishing skin as the site of origin.
High-grade renal epithelial carcinoma with sarcomatoid differentiation; sarcomatoid morphology does not establish muscle or bone origin.
Immune-mediated necrotizing lymphadenitis; supplied HPO lists oral ulcers, alopecia/cutaneous vasculitis and vasculitis at 30-79%. Transient rash alone is excluded.
Mechanical inability to close the eyelids; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Atherosclerotic disease directly affects the aortic wall; downstream ischemic diseases are not assumed.
Inherited ELOVL4-related macular dystrophy with macular atrophy and impaired vision.
CARD11-associated dominant-negative immune dysfunction; severe atopic dermatitis affects roughly 80-90%. Separately diagnosed respiratory infections are excluded.
